option.name: --abbrev
tip: Abbreviate the output of the system calls in SET.
SET has the same syntax as --trace.

option.name: --absolute-timestamps
tip: Prefix each line with the wall clock time.
FORMAT is none, time, or unix; PRECISION is s, ms, us, or ns.
Use format:VALUE and precision:VALUE, joined by a comma. (default format:time,precision:s)
The value must be attached with '='.

option.name: --always-show-pid
tip: Show the PID prefix also for the process started by strace.
Implied when -f and -o are both given.

option.name: --arg-names
tip: Print system call argument names.

option.name: --argv0
tip: Set argv[0] of the traced command to NAME.

option.name: --attach
tip: Attach to the process with process ID PID.
May be repeated; one value can list multiple PIDs separated by comma, space, tab, or newline.

option.name: --color
tip: Colorize the output.
WHEN is auto, always, or never. (default auto)

option.name: --columns
tip: Set the alignment column for printing system call results. (default 40)

option.name: --const-print-style
tip: Set the format for printing named constants and flags. (default abbrev)

option.name: --daemonize
tip: Run the tracer as a grandchild of the tracee.
MODE is grandchild, pgroup, pgrp, or session. (default grandchild)
The value must be attached with '='.

option.name: --debug
tip: Enable debug output on standard error.

option.name: --decode-fds
tip: Print file descriptor information for the kinds in SET.
SET is a comma-separated list of: path, socket, dev, eventfd, pidfd, signalfd.
Use all or none for the whole set.
The value must be attached with '='; the bare flag means path.

option.name: --decode-pids
tip: Print additional information associated with PIDs.
SET is a comma-separated list of comm, pidns, all, or none.

option.name: --detach-on
tip: Detach from the tracee when SYSCALL is reached.
Currently only execve is supported.

option.name: --env
tip: Set VAR=VAL in the environment of the traced command.
Use VAR alone to remove the variable from the environment.

option.name: --failed-only
tip: Print only system calls that returned an error.

option.name: --fault
tip: Inject a fault into the system calls in SET.
SET uses the same syntax as --trace.
This is a shortcut for --inject with a default error of ENOSYS.

option.name: --follow-forks
tip: Follow child processes created by fork, vfork, and clone.

option.name: --help
tip: Print the help summary.

option.name: --inject
tip: Perform syscall tampering for the system calls in SET.
SET uses the same syntax as --trace.
Actions: error=ERRNO, retval=VALUE, signal=SIG, syscall=SYSCALL, delay_enter=DELAY, delay_exit=DELAY, poke_enter=@argN=DATA, poke_exit=@argN=DATA, when=FIRST[..LAST][+[STEP]].

option.name: --instruction-pointer
tip: Print the instruction pointer at the time of the system call.

option.name: --interruptible
tip: Control when strace can be interrupted by signals.
MODE is 1/anywhere, 2/waiting, 3/never, or 4/never_tstp.

option.name: --kill-on-exit
tip: Kill all tracees when the tracer exits.
Not compatible with -p/--attach.

option.name: --kvm
tip: Print the exit reason of a KVM vCPU.
Append + to also print the kvm_run structure.

option.name: --namespace
tip: Print namespace IDs that the tracee enters.
The only value is new.
The value must be attached with '='.

option.name: --no-abbrev
tip: Print unabbreviated versions of environment, stat, termios, and other structures.

option.name: --output
tip: Send trace output to FILE instead of standard error.

option.name: --output-append-mode
tip: Open the file given to -o in append mode.

option.name: --output-separately
tip: Write each process's trace to a separate FILE.PID file.
Requires -o/--output.

option.name: --pidns-translation
tip: Deprecated: use --decode-pids=pidns instead.
Print PIDs in strace's PID namespace.

option.name: --raw
tip: Print undecoded arguments for the system calls in SET.
SET has the same syntax as --trace.

option.name: --read
tip: Dump the data read from the file descriptors in SET.
SET is a comma-separated list of file descriptor numbers.

option.name: --relative-timestamps
tip: Print a relative timestamp on entry to each system call.
PRECISION is s, ms, us, or ns. (default us)
The value must be attached with '='.

option.name: --seccomp-bpf
tip: Use seccomp-bpf to stop the tracee only for the system calls being traced.
Requires -f/--follow-forks; incompatible with --syscall-limit and -b/--detach-on.

option.name: --secontext
tip: Print SELinux contexts of processes, files, and descriptors.
(SELinux-enabled builds only)
FORMAT is a comma-separated list of full and mismatch; prefix an item with ! to disable it.
The value must be attached with '='; the default is !full,mismatch.

option.name: --signals
tip: Trace only the specified set of signals.
SET is a comma-separated list of signal names or numbers; all and none are accepted.
Prefix a value with ! to negate it.

option.name: --silence
tip: Suppress various informational messages.
SET is a comma-separated list of: attach, exit, path-resolution, personality, thread-execve, superseded.
Use all or none for the whole set.
The value must be attached with '='; the bare flag suppresses attach and personality.

option.name: --status
tip: Print only system calls with the return status in SET.
Possible values: successful, failed, unfinished, unavailable, detached.
Use all or none for the whole set.

option.name: --string-limit
tip: Limit the length of printed strings to STRSIZE characters. (default 32)

option.name: --strings-in-hex
tip: Control hexadecimal escape sequences when printing strings.
MODE is none, non-ascii-chars, non-ascii, or all. (default none)
The value must be attached with '='; the bare flag means all.

option.name: --successful-only
tip: Print only system calls that returned without an error.

option.name: --summary
tip: Like -c, but also print the regular output.

option.name: --summary-columns
tip: Show the listed columns in the summary report.
COLUMNS is a comma-separated list of: time-percent, total-time, min-time, max-time, avg-time, calls, errors, name.
The default is time-percent,total-time,avg-time,calls,errors,name.
Used with -c/--summary-only or -C/--summary.

option.name: --summary-only
tip: Count time, calls, and errors for each system call and print a summary.
Suppresses the regular output.

option.name: --summary-sort-by
tip: Sort the summary by SORTBY. (default time)
Used with -c/--summary-only or -C/--summary.

option.name: --summary-syscall-overhead
tip: Set the overhead for tracing system calls to OVERHEAD UNITs.
UNIT is s, ms, us, or ns. (default us)
Used with -c/--summary-only or -C/--summary.

option.name: --summary-wall-clock
tip: Summarize syscall latency using wall clock time instead of system time.
Used with -c/--summary-only or -C/--summary.

option.name: --syscall-limit
tip: Detach all tracees after tracing LIMIT system calls.

option.name: --syscall-number
tip: Print the system call number.

option.name: --syscall-times
tip: Print the time spent in each system call.
PRECISION is s, ms, us, or ns. (default us)
The value must be attached with '='.

option.name: --tips
tip: Show strace tips, tricks, and tweaks on exit.
VALUE is [[id:]ID][,[format:]FORMAT]; ID is a non-negative integer or random.
FORMAT is none, compact, or full. (default id:random,format:compact)
The value must be attached with '='.

option.name: --trace
tip: Trace only the specified set of system calls.
SET is a comma-separated list of syscall names, %group names, all, none, or /REGEX.
Prefix a value with ! to negate it and with ? to suppress errors for unmatched syscalls.
Groups: %clock, %creds, %desc, %file, %fstat, %fstatfs, %ipc, %lstat, %memory, %net, %network, %process, %pure, %signal, %stat, %%stat, %statfs, %%statfs.
Common syscalls are listed as examples; any syscall name is accepted.

next.name: %%stat
tip: All file-status system calls.

next.name: %%statfs
tip: All filesystem-statistics system calls.

next.name: %clock
tip: System calls that read or modify system clocks.

next.name: %creds
tip: System calls that read or modify user/group IDs or capabilities.

next.name: %desc
tip: File-descriptor-related system calls.

next.name: %file
tip: System calls that take a file name.

next.name: %fstat
tip: fstat, fstatat, and statx variants.

next.name: %fstatfs
tip: fstatfs and fstatvfs variants.

next.name: %ipc
tip: IPC-related system calls.

next.name: %lstat
tip: lstat variants.

next.name: %memory
tip: Memory-mapping-related system calls.

next.name: %net
tip: Network-related system calls.

next.name: %network
tip: Alias for %net.

next.name: %process
tip: Process lifecycle system calls.

next.name: %pure
tip: System calls that always succeed and take no arguments.

next.name: %signal
tip: Signal-related system calls.

next.name: %stat
tip: stat variants.

next.name: %statfs
tip: statfs and statvfs variants.

next.name: all
tip: All system calls.

next.name: none
tip: No system calls.

option.name: --trace-fds
tip: Trace operations on file descriptors in SET.
SET is a comma-separated list of file descriptor numbers.

option.name: --trace-path
tip: Trace accesses to PATH.

option.name: --user
tip: Run the command as USERNAME.
USERNAME may be a user name or a UID:GID pair.
Only useful when strace runs as root.

option.name: --verbose
tip: Dereference structures for the system calls in SET.
SET has the same syntax as --trace.

option.name: --version
tip: Print version information.

option.name: --write
tip: Dump the data written to the file descriptors in SET.
SET is a comma-separated list of file descriptor numbers.

option.name: -D
tip: Run the tracer as a grandchild of the tracee.
Equivalent to --daemonize=grandchild.

option.name: -DD
tip: Run the tracer as a grandchild in a separate process group.
Equivalent to --daemonize=pgroup.

option.name: -DDD
tip: Run the tracer as a grandchild in a separate session.
Equivalent to --daemonize=session.

option.name: -e
tip: Modify which events to trace or how they are traced.
EXPR is QUALIFIER=[!]VALUE[,VALUE]...; the default qualifier is trace.
Qualifiers: trace, trace-fds, abbrev, verbose, raw, signal, read, write, fault, inject, status, quiet, secontext, kvm, namespace, decode-fds, decode-pids.
Qualifier aliases: t, trace-fd, fd, fds, a, v, x, signals, s, reads, r, writes, w, q, silent, silence, decode-fd, decode-pid.

option.name: -F
tip: Deprecated: use -f/--follow-forks instead.
Retained for backward compatibility; ignored when -f is also given.

option.name: -ff
tip: Follow forks and write each process's trace to a separate output file.
Equivalent to -f --output-separately.

option.name: -q
tip: Suppress attach, detach, and personality messages.
Equivalent to --quiet=attach,personality.

option.name: -qq
tip: Suppress attach, detach, personality, and exit messages.
Equivalent to --quiet=attach,personality,exit.

option.name: -qqq
tip: Suppress all suppressible messages.
Equivalent to --quiet=all.

option.name: -r
tip: Print a relative timestamp on entry to each system call with microsecond precision.
Equivalent to --relative-timestamps=us.

option.name: -t
tip: Prefix each line with the wall clock time.
Equivalent to --absolute-timestamps=format:time,precision:s.

option.name: -T
tip: Print the time spent in each system call with microsecond precision.
Equivalent to --syscall-times=us.

option.name: -tt
tip: Print the wall clock time with microsecond precision.
Equivalent to --absolute-timestamps=precision:us.

option.name: -ttt
tip: Print the wall clock time as seconds since the epoch with microsecond precision.
Equivalent to --absolute-timestamps=format:unix,precision:us.

option.name: -x
tip: Print non-ASCII strings in hexadecimal.
Equivalent to --strings-in-hex=non-ascii.

option.name: -xx
tip: Print all strings in hexadecimal.
Equivalent to --strings-in-hex=all.

option.name: -y
tip: Print paths associated with file descriptor arguments.
Equivalent to --decode-fds=path.

option.name: -Y
tip: Print command names associated with PIDs.
Equivalent to --decode-pids=comm.

option.name: -yy
tip: Print all available information associated with file descriptors.
Equivalent to --decode-fds=all.
